range.summary: Large rivers of the Mississippi–Missouri–Ohio basin and neighbouring Gulf of Mexico drainages, central and southern USA

funFact: Its paddle-shaped snout stretches nearly a third of its body length and is covered with tens of thousands of sensory receptors for finding swarms of zooplankton.
revealFact: Native to the Mississippi River basin and neighbouring Gulf Coast drainages, it is the last living paddlefish, since its only modern relative, from China's Yangtze, is considered extinct. Overfishing, habitat destruction, pollution and poaching have shrunk its range.

hints.habitat: Slow-flowing big rivers, backwaters, oxbow lakes and reservoirs
hints.size: Up to about 221 cm (2.2 m) long
hints.diet: Plankton, mainly zooplankton, filtered from the water

range.summary: Three lakes of the Petite Rivière system (Hebb, Milipsigate, Minamkeak), Lunenburg County, Nova Scotia; formerly also the Tusket River

funFact: Its lineage split from all other whitefish about 15 million years ago, and nobody has ever seen it reproduce in the wild.
revealFact: It survives only as landlocked populations in lakes of the Petite Rivière watershed in Nova Scotia; sea-run fish in the Tusket and Annis rivers are gone. Dams and introduced predators such as smallmouth bass and chain pickerel made it critically endangered.

hints.habitat: Open water of freshwater lakes; historically also migrated between rivers and coastal estuaries
hints.size: Up to about 40 cm long
hints.diet: Insects and small fish

range.summary: Eastern North Pacific from the Gulf of Alaska to central Baja California, most common off California

funFact: A single female can produce over 2 million eggs a season, releasing her young as live larvae rather than laying eggs. Juveniles hide under floating kelp mats, driftwood and even oil platforms.
revealFact: The bocaccio ranges along the eastern North Pacific from Alaska to central Baja California, and is most abundant from Oregon to northern Baja California. It can live at least 50 years and is critically endangered.

hints.habitat: Rocky reefs and open bottoms; young shelter near shore under floating kelp
hints.size: Up to about 91 cm long
hints.diet: Mainly fish, including other rockfish; young eat zooplankton such as copepods

range.summary: High-elevation Golden Trout Creek and the South Fork Kern River in the southern Sierra Nevada, Tulare County, California

verification.notes: FishBase native/endemic: US | IUCN NE; tiny range: Golden Trout Creek, Volcano Creek and the South Fork Kern River only

funFact: Its golden flanks are striped with red bands and about ten dark oval 'parr marks' on each side, and its fins have white leading edges.
revealFact: It is native to the southern Sierra Nevada of California, in Golden Trout Creek, Volcano Creek and the South Fork Kern River. It has been California's official state freshwater fish since 1947.

hints.habitat: Clear, cool mountain headwaters, creeks and lakes above about 2,100 m elevation
hints.size: Up to about 71 cm long

range.summary: Richelieu River and nearby stretches of the St Lawrence and its tributaries in south-western Quebec, Canada

funFact: Unlike its relatives, it has molar-like throat teeth for crushing hard-shelled bivalves, and it shows off a bright red tail fin.
revealFact: It is found only in south-western Quebec, in the St Lawrence and Richelieu rivers and the Rivière des Mille Îles, and its tiny range has shrunk sharply in recent decades.

hints.habitat: Rocky pools, backwaters and runs of medium-sized rivers that warm above 20 °C in summer
hints.size: Up to about 72 cm long

hints.diet: Hard-shelled bivalves

range.summary: The Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta, Suisun Bay and Suisun Marsh, California

photo.author: Peterson, B. Moose / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

revealFact: It is endemic to the upper Sacramento–San Joaquin estuary of California, where large-scale water pumping and habitat loss have left it functionally extinct in the wild.

hints.habitat: Open, low-salinity channels of an estuary where fresh and salt water mix
hints.size: Up to about 12 cm long
hints.diet: Zooplankton

range.summary: A single water-filled limestone fissure, Devils Hole, in the Ash Meadows area of Nye County, Nevada

hints.habitat: The upper waters of one deep, water-filled limestone cavern, around a shallow rock ledge
hints.size: Up to about 3.4 cm long
hints.diet: Nearly everything on offer: beetles, snails, algae and small freshwater crustaceans

range.summary: Lower Elk River, West Virginia: the only known surviving population

funFact: It is named for the sparkle it reflects when scientists collect it at night, and its see-through body is patterned in olive.
revealFact: Once recorded from several Ohio River tributaries, including the Cumberland, Green and Muskingum, it is now known only from the Elk River in West Virginia. It was listed as endangered in 2013.

hints.habitat: The tail ends of riffles and heads of pools, with moderate flow over sand, gravel and cobble
hints.size: Up to about 7.7 cm long (standard length)

range.summary: Eastern North Pacific from Humboldt Bay, California, to southern Baja California and the northern Gulf of California, mostly around Southern California and Baja

revealFact: It survives in just six population centres in the Colorado River system, including the Grand Canyon and the Little Colorado River in Arizona and canyons in Utah and Colorado. Habitat loss, such as from Glen Canyon Dam, cut its numbers dramatically.

hints.habitat: Swift, rocky runs and turbulent pools in steep, high-gradient stretches of large rivers

revealFact: It lives only in spring-fed wetlands of northern Alabama, chiefly the Beaverdam Spring complex in Limestone County, with a second population found in 2015 at Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge.

hints.habitat: Clear spring heads, spring pools and their weedy, spring-fed wetlands

revealFact: It lives only in Lake Apoyo, a volcanic crater lake in Nicaragua, where genetic evidence suggests it and five close relatives evolved side by side within the same lake.

hints.habitat: A single volcanic crater lake
hints.size: Up to about 20 cm long

range.summary: Flooded caves and cenotes of the northern Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico

funFact: Its describer loved giving cave fish devilish names, so he first called it Pluto infernalis, from the Latin for Hell. It has no eyes, no scales and no pigment.
revealFact: It is endemic to water-filled sinkholes and limestone caves of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, turning up in only about 7% of caves searched. Sewage and wastewater seeping into the aquifer threaten it.

revealFact: It comes from the upper Río Ameca basin around Teuchitlán in Jalisco, Mexico, historically an area only about 15 km across. Once an aquarium favourite, it is now rated critically endangered by the IUCN.

hints.habitat: Springs and small streams of hard, alkaline water over limestone bedrock
hints.size: Up to about 8 cm long

revealFact: The Clarion damselfish ranges from Mexico's Revillagigedo Islands to the southern tip of Baja California, but about 95% of the population lives around the Revillagigedo Islands. Warm El Niño events could threaten it, and it is listed as vulnerable.

hints.habitat: Rocky inshore reefs

range.summary: Lowland rivers, lagoons and swamps of western Cuba (notably the Zapata Swamp) and Isla de la Juventud

revealFact: It lives in rivers, lakes and swamps of western Cuba, including the Zapata Swamp, and on the Isla de la Juventud. Overfishing, habitat loss and introduced largemouth bass, which prey on its young, have made it critically endangered.

hints.habitat: Slow rivers, lakes and floodplains; it also tolerates brackish water
hints.size: Up to about 200 cm (2 m) long
hints.diet: Other fish and even birds

range.summary: Eastern Pacific from Baja California into the Gulf of California and south to Mazatlán (historically north to Southern California)

revealFact: It is endemic to Mexican waters from Baja California Sur south to Mazatlán, including the whole Gulf of California and the Revillagigedo Islands. Commercial fishing has cut its numbers sharply since the mid-20th century.

hints.habitat: Rocky reefs, kelp beds and seamounts
hints.size: Up to about 198 cm (2 m) long
hints.diet: Fish, lobsters and slipper lobsters, even young hammerhead sharks

revealFact: The humpbacked limia lives only in Lake Miragoâne in Haiti, which suffers from severe deforestation, pollution and climate change. With no species-specific protection in place, it is critically endangered.

hints.habitat: A lake with weedy, muddy shallows; schools over all kinds of bottoms
hints.size: Up to about 5.2 cm long (body length, tail fin excluded)

revealFact: It is endemic to the spring pools of the butterfly-shaped Cuatro Ciénegas basin in Coahuila, Mexico, a place with very high levels of endemism. It honours ichthyologist Wendell Minckley, who studied the basin's ecology.

hints.habitat: Clear spring-fed pools with plant and rock cover in a very dry basin
hints.size: Up to about 17.5 cm long (standard length)
hints.diet: Snails and small fish

revealFact: It is native to just a few springs and streams of the upper Río Tunal around Durango, Mexico, such as the Abraham González spring and the El Salto waterfall area. Invasive species keep threatening its tiny range.

revealFact: It is endemic to the Ameca River basin in Jalisco, Mexico, and by the early 2000s survived only in one tiny spring pool at Teuchitlán. After years of reintroduction work it now thrives at home again, and its name comes from the nearby Tequila Volcano.

hints.size: Up to about 6 cm long

revealFact: The Banggai cardinalfish is naturally restricted to the shallows of the Banggai Archipelago off Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, where an estimated 2.4 million fish share about 5,500 km². Heavy collection for the aquarium trade and disease have made it Endangered.

revealFact: Betta persephone is known only from Johor in Peninsular Malaysia, with its type locality in the peat swamp forest at Ayer Hitam. Its small swampy range is shrinking as forests are cleared for oil palm plantations.

revealFact: The cave angelfish is known from eight caves in the Pang Mapha karst of Mae Hong Son Province, northern Thailand, occupying only about 6 km². Agricultural pollution, deforestation and caving tourism threaten its fragile cave streams.

revealFact: The Canterbury mudfish (kowaro) lives only on the Canterbury Plains of New Zealand's South Island, from just north of Christchurch to the Waitaki River. Its wetlands were largely drained for farming, so it now clings on in springs, water races and drains.

hints.habitat: Wetlands, springs and drains that can dry out over summer
hints.size: Up to about 15 cm long

range.summary: Peaty streams and wetlands of Southland and Stewart Island (Rakiura), New Zealand

funFact: This scaleless little fish has big eyes set high on its head, each wider than 23% of its head length. It also packs enlarged canine teeth in both jaws.
revealFact: The Gollum galaxias lives only in southern New Zealand: streams of the Southland Plains, tributaries of the Clutha River, the Catlins and Stewart Island / Rakiura. It belongs to a group of 10 species that were once all lumped together as a single species.

hints.habitat: Slow or still lowland streams and wetlands, among moss, woody debris and plant-lined banks
hints.size: The type specimen measured about 7.5 cm long

range.summary: Lake Kutubu and its outflow, Southern Highlands, Papua New Guinea

funFact: Nicknamed the turquoise rainbowfish, it shares its one home lake with 12 other fish species found nowhere else on Earth.
revealFact: The Lake Kutubu rainbowfish lives only in Lake Kutubu and its outflow in the Southern Highlands of Papua New Guinea, part of the Kikori River system. It is one of 13 fish species endemic to the lake and is listed as endangered.

hints.habitat: A highland lake and its outlet stream, far upstream from the sea
hints.size: Up to about 10 cm long (body length, tail fin excluded)
hints.diet: Omnivorous

range.summary: Lake Wanam, a small lake in the Markham valley near Lae, Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea

funFact: Its whole natural home is one small lake just 2–3 km across, where introduced tilapia have nearly wiped it out. Luckily, captive populations keep the species going.
revealFact: The Lake Wanam rainbowfish is endemic to Lake Wanam near Lae in Papua New Guinea. Competition from introduced tilapias has made it critically endangered, and it has virtually vanished from the wild.

hints.habitat: A small lake about 150 m above sea level
hints.size: Up to about 9 cm long (body length, tail fin excluded)
hints.diet: Omnivorous

range.summary: Shallow reefs of eastern Papua New Guinea, especially Milne Bay Province

funFact: Covered in dense leopard-like spots with a big black eyespot behind its head, this little shark went unrecognised until 2010, when a photographer noticed it was different and it was named after him.
revealFact: The leopard epaulette shark is known only from shallow reefs of eastern Papua New Guinea, mostly in Milne Bay Province. It was long confused with the Indonesian speckled carpetshark until it was described as a separate species in 2010.

hints.habitat: Coral reefs, rocky outcrops, tide pools and seagrass beds
hints.size: Up to about 70 cm long

revealFact: The northern river shark is found in scattered tidal rivers and coastal waters of northern Australia (the Kimberley and the Northern Territory) and southern Papua New Guinea. Very rare, it is threatened by commercial and recreational fishing.

hints.habitat: Murky tidal rivers, estuaries and coastal bays with muddy bottoms

revealFact: Once found at several sites around south-east Tasmania, the red handfish is now known from just two small reefs in Frederick Henry Bay, each no more than about 50 m across. Its slow breeding and dispersal keep its range tiny, and it is critically endangered.

funFact: Males blaze bright red and grow a taller back with age, though low-ranking males stay drab. Its scientific name is almost always misspelt: grammar demands 'incisa', not 'incisus'.
revealFact: The red rainbowfish is found only in Lake Sentani and its tributaries near Jayapura in Papua, Indonesia. A fast-growing human population around the lake and introduced fish such as tilapia have made it endangered.

hints.habitat: A lake in hilly country about 75 m above sea level, and its tributaries
hints.size: Up to about 12 cm long (body length, tail fin excluded)
hints.diet: Omnivorous, possibly a bit more meat-loving than its relatives

range.summary: Lower Derwent Estuary and nearby bays of south-east Tasmania, Australia

funFact: Its hand-shaped fins let it stroll across the seafloor instead of swimming. Females lay eggs on upright objects such as sea squirts and seagrass, and the young hatch 7–8 weeks later as fully formed mini handfish.
revealFact: The spotted handfish lives only in the Derwent Estuary of south-east Tasmania, Australia, and nearby areas. It is critically endangered, chiefly threatened by an invasive species, the Northern Pacific seastar.

hints.habitat: Sandy bottoms in sheltered inshore waters, often in shell-filled hollows
hints.size: Up to about 15 cm long

funFact: Disguised with leafy flaps that mimic seaweed, it drifts rather than swims and can't grip with its tail like a seahorse. Dad carries around 120 eggs stuck under his tail for about a month.
revealFact: The weedy seadragon lives only along Australia's temperate southern coast, from Western Australia to New South Wales and around Tasmania. It is the marine emblem of the state of Victoria.

hints.habitat: Rocky reefs, kelp and seaweed beds and seagrass meadows
hints.size: Up to about 46 cm long

revealFact: White's seahorse, also called the Sydney seahorse, lives in estuaries and sheltered bays of central New South Wales, from Port Stephens to the Sydney area. As its natural seagrass and sponge habitats disappear, it increasingly uses jetties and other artificial structures.

hints.habitat: Sheltered bays among seagrass, sponges, soft corals and kelp, and under jetties

revealFact: The black-striped salema lives only in the waters around the Galápagos Islands, where it was first described in 1890 from Isla Santa María.

hints.habitat: Rock walls and rocky slopes, in big daytime schools

revealFact: The Clipperton angelfish lives only around Clipperton Island, a remote French atoll in the eastern Pacific west of Costa Rica. Its isolation makes it extremely scarce in the aquarium trade, where it fetches very high prices.

revealFact: The Cocos barnacle blenny lives only in the waters around Cocos Island (Isla del Coco), Costa Rica.

hints.habitat: On the bottom of rocky reefs; common in the shallows

range.summary: Lord Howe Island, Norfolk Island and the Middleton and Elizabeth reefs, with rare visitors to the New South Wales coast

revealFact: The doubleheader lives around Lord Howe Island, Norfolk Island and Middleton Reef in the south-west Pacific, only rarely turning up off New South Wales. Usually seen in small groups dominated by one large male, it is listed as vulnerable.

funFact: These groupers appear to start adult life as females and switch to male around age 12. Every so often one shows up entirely bright yellow instead of the usual spotted grey-brown.
revealFact: The Galápagos (sailfin) grouper lives off the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador, with smaller populations at Cocos Island (Costa Rica) and Malpelo Island (Colombia). It is the most valuable finfish landed by the islands' handline fishery and is now endangered.

revealFact: The Malpelo barnacle blenny is found only on reefs around Malpelo Island, Colombia, in the eastern Pacific.

funFact: Each group is ruled by its biggest fish, the female; if she dies, the breeding male turns female and the next-largest steps up. It lives with just one kind of anemone, the bubble-tip.
revealFact: McCulloch's anemonefish lives only around Lord Howe Island and the nearby Middleton and Elizabeth reefs in the south-western Pacific. Its tiny range and reliance on a single kind of anemone make it vulnerable.

revealFact: The nopili rock-climbing goby is endemic to the Hawaiian Islands, living in clear, fast mountain streams on all the main islands, though it is now rare on Oahu. Its larvae drift out to sea, and juveniles must climb back past towering waterfalls to reach upstream pools.

revealFact: ʻOʻopu nākea lives only in streams of the main Hawaiian Islands. Once lumped in with a related goby, it was recognised as a distinct species thanks to differences in body form and genetics.

revealFact: The red-striped wrasse is found only around Cocos Island (Isla del Coco), Costa Rica; close relatives fill the same sandy-rubble niche on the mainland and at Malpelo Island.

revealFact: The West Indian Ocean coelacanth lives on deep rocky slopes mainly around the Comoros (Grande Comore and Anjouan), with smaller populations off South Africa, Mozambique, Tanzania, Kenya and Madagascar.
